identity.title: One Step Diffusion via Shortcut Models

problem.claim: Accelerate diffusion and flow-matching image generation, which otherwise requires many iterative denoising passes.

gap.claim: Existing acceleration methods rely on complex training setups involving multiple phases, networks, or fragile scheduling.

contributions.claim: Introduces Shortcut Models, using one network and one training phase to generate samples in one or multiple steps.
Conditions generation on both noise level and desired step size, enabling inference-time step skipping and variable step budgets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Shortcut Models by combining single-network, single-phase training with variable inference-time step budgets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistently higher-quality samples than consistency models and reflow across a wide range of sampling step budgets.
The authors report lower complexity than distillation—one network and one training phase—while retaining variable step budgets at inference.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion and flow-matching models generate realistic, diverse images by transferring noise to data.
Their iterative denoising makes sampling slow and expensive, while prior acceleration methods use complex training regimes.
Shortcut Models use a single network and training phase; conditioning on desired step size lets the model skip ahead.
The authors report stronger sample quality across step budgets than consistency models and reflow, plus lower complexity and flexible budgets relative to distillation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a model's step-size conditioning directly to both skipping generation steps and varying inference budgets.

lessons.interpretation: A design feature is more persuasive when its mechanism is connected to the operational flexibility it enables.
lessons.application: When presenting an acceleration method, map each architectural or conditioning choice to a concrete inference-time control and state the comparison baseline.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method's main contribution is theoretical or resource-based rather than an inference mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, quality metrics, numerical gains, compute costs, or the precise comparison protocols.
It does not establish whether the reported quality advantage holds uniformly for every step budget or setting.
